title: Agent swarm registry
description: One registry file per swarm run. A swarm is N headless Claude CLI workers, each with a private sandbox and a task list. Workers are generic: nothing in the schema is specific to one job. The number of workers and tasks is whatever the operator asks for.

swarm_id.description: Kebab-case id, also the run folder name under runs/.

brief_path.description: Shared rules file every worker must read first (for example the no-guessing rules).

model.description: Alias passed to claude --model. Always pass it explicitly; never rely on the CLI default. Verified on CLI 2.1.224: sonnet resolves to claude-sonnet-5, haiku resolves to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, fable and opus also exist and are expensive.

max_budget_usd.description: Passed to --max-budget-usd. Optional hard stop per worker.

permission_mode.description: Safe only because the sandbox is a private folder and deny rules protect everything else.

add_dirs.description: Extra directories the worker may read.

deny_tools.description: Passed to --disallowedTools. Note: write protection uses Edit(path) rules, Write(path) is not matched.

sandbox.description: Absolute path of the only folder this worker may write to. Persistent: a later task reuses the same folder and its clones and notes.

runtime.description: Overrides swarm defaults for this worker.

state_detail.description: Short human text for what the worker is doing right now, derived from its last event.

session_id.description: Claude session UUID, lets a later task resume with --resume.

model_seen.description: Model name read from the stream events, to verify the requested model was really used.

stream_log.description: Full raw event stream, one JSON event per line. Nothing is dropped. Use it to reassess a worker after the fact or while it is still running.

activities.description: Live activity feed: rolling window of the latest human-readable steps taken from the worker stream (reasoning, tool calls, tool results, text), newest last. Capped so the registry stays small. The complete stream is in stream_log.

_offset.description: Watcher bookkeeping: byte offset already consumed from the stream log.

_result_error.description: Watcher bookkeeping: the final result event reported is_error.

_result_text.description: Watcher bookkeeping: first 300 chars of the final result text.

stream_format.description: plain-text marks legacy logs from before the watcher existed; they are never parsed.

workerStatus.description: idle: no task running, sandbox kept. starting: process launched, no event yet. researching: tool calls in flight (search, fetch, shell, git). thinking: model reasoning. writing: writing a file. waiting: blocked on rate limit or retry. stalled: no event for stall_after_seconds. rate_limited: provider said stop. done/failed/stopped: terminal for the current task, worker can accept a new task.

prompt.description: Exactly what the worker is told for this task. Include inputs (paths) and the expected output file.

expected_outputs.description: Paths, relative to the sandbox. The task is only marked done when they exist and are non-empty.

status.description: queued: waiting. running: current task. done: outputs exist and verified. partial: ended with some outputs or hit a limit. failed: ended with error. blocked: cannot start (dependency or limit). unknown: process gone, outcome not verified yet. skipped: operator cancelled.

result_note.description: One or two lines: what was verified, what is missing.

qa.description: Independent quality check of this task's output, done by the operator's own session and not by the worker. Optional. A task whose qa.status is complete is skipped when the operator asks to validate; only pending or in_progress tasks are checked.

status.description: pending: not checked yet. in_progress: some checks recorded, more planned. complete: no more checks will be done for this task.

checked_by.description: Who ran the checks, for example the model name of the operator session.

tally.description: Counts of check verdicts. Score = confirmed / (confirmed + corrected + wrong). Inconclusive checks are excluded from the denominator because they reflect a limit of the checker (rate limit, no access), not an error by the worker.

entry.description: Which item of the task output this check is about, for example a catalog entry name.

claim.description: What the worker asserted, in one line.

observed_value.description: What the operator's independent check actually found.

verdict.description: confirmed: matches. corrected: partly right, a detail needed fixing. wrong: the claim was false. inconclusive: could not be checked.

evidence.description: Command, URL or file the check used, so it can be repeated.
